highlights.text: cheap gaming laptop with a good keyboard
2 hours 16 minutes on the RTX 5050 model

paras: Reviewers mostly like it as a cheap, sturdy ThinkPad with a comfortable keyboard and room to upgrade RAM and SSDs, suited to office, school and budget buyers, though the screens measured show weak colour coverage. Battery results vary by config and test: the Core Ultra 7 155U model managed 9h 26min of WiFi browsing (Notebookcheck) but only 5 hours 36 minutes in the PCMark 10 battery test (XDA Developers), while the Ryzen 5 7535HS version ran nearly 19 hours of video and browsing but cut its CPU power after 30 to 45 minutes (TECHSETTER). Against its siblings, the Intel model is preferred over the AMD version this year because the AMD one uses a previous generation CPU (Tech Guy Beau), while the Ryzen 7 7735HS model's Radeon 680M scored almost 86 percent higher in 3DMark than the E14 Gen 5 AMD (Notebookcheck, German review).

highlights.text: room to upgrade RAM and SSDs

paras: Reviewers mostly pitch it as an office laptop and praise the keyboard, with Tech Guy Beau calling it a superb typing experience. The screen splits opinion by config: Tech Guy Beau liked the 1600p panel and Notebookcheck measured 410 nits on the WQHD option, while PCMag Australia called the 1920 by 1200 Intel model's screen dim and bland, and TechRadar measured 54% sRGB on its Ryzen 5 7530U unit. Battery runs from about 3.5 hours of general use on the Core i5-1335U model (How-To Geek) to over 11 hours on the Ryzen 7 7730U WQHD model (Notebookcheck), and the Acer TravelMate P4 TMP416-51-55KN offers similar performance with more modern ports (Notebookcheck).

Reviewers praise the keyboard and the port selection, with Tech Guy Beau calling the keyboard best in class on the Ryzen 7 7735U model and Notebookcheck rating it strong on the Ryzen 5 7535U model. Mixed takes come mostly from the screen: Tech Guy Beau recommends the optional 100% sRGB 1200p panel, while Hendrik Widarmawan found the Core Ultra 7 155U model's panel not fully sRGB and Notebookcheck measured 56.1% sRGB on the Ryzen 5 7535U model. Notebookcheck also recorded 12h 28min of Wi-Fi web surfing on that Ryzen 5 model, but noted coil whine and a plastic chassis, and says the HP ProBook 445 G10 is cheaper and lighter but lacks USB4 and WWAN (Notebookcheck).

Reviewers mostly suit it to editors, developers and other professionals who want a portable workstation, praising the keyboard and speakers, and Laptop Mag recorded 17 hours 23 minutes of web surfing on the Core Ultra 7 165H, RTX 1000 Ada IPS model. Performance is where takes split, as the RTX 4060 version holds about 60W in games against 80W on the Gen 6 (Mash IT) and runs hot and loud, while the 4060 model also drops the Gen 6's high-end GPU options (Notebookcheck). Many reviewers liked the haptic trackpad, but LongRhino disliked it, HAMY LABS found it oversensitive, and several reviewers called the price high.

Reviewers like the keyboard, the 120Hz screen and the two SO-DIMM slots, and Slap Tech and Tech Guy Beau both loved it, the former at about $1,500 for the Core Ultra 7 155H and RTX 500 version. Takes are mixed at Notebookcheck, which measured 46.8 dB(A) fan noise and about 60 W of sustained cooling on the Intel model, and 50.8 dB(A) plus 6h 11min of Wi-Fi battery life on the Ryzen 7 Pro 8840HS OLED model, where the T14 Gen 5 AMD is the better choice for most users (Notebookcheck). Slap Tech says the 2022 Asus Zephyrus G14 wins on gaming and ghosting but runs hotter than the ThinkPad (Slap Tech), while Tech Guy Beau found the AMD model scoring about 14,000 in Cinebench against about 12,000 for the Gen 4 (Tech Guy Beau).

It suits office users, students and ThinkPad fans who want a light, repairable machine, with the keyboard praised by reviewers including XDA Developers and Notebookcheck. Mixed takes come mostly from battery life, which depends on the config: the Core Ultra 7 155U model with 16GB ran 10 hours 48 minutes in a PCMark 10 test (XDA Developers) but 7:27 to 8:44 in a web-surfing test (Laptop Mag), and the Ryzen models ranged from 6 hours 20 minutes of YouTube streaming (Mash IT) to 10 hours 15 minutes in a Wi-Fi test (Notebookcheck). On comparisons, the Ryzen 7 8840U version was faster than the Intel T14 Gen 5 in CPU and graphics (Notebookcheck), and the Acer Swift 14 AI and MacBook Pro 14-inch last longer (Laptop Mag).

Reviewers pitch it as a business ThinkPad for office work, with ThinkView praising the curved keys and solid carbon fiber build and Notebookcheck praising the cool case and almost twelve hours of Wi-Fi battery life on the Core Ultra 5 125U model. Battery depends on the config: ThinkView reports nearly 7 hours at 250 nits on the Core Ultra 155U version, against Notebookcheck's 11h 52min at 150 nits on a low-power 1920x1200 panel. On speed, the integrated graphics in the HP EliteBook 845 G10 are about 20 per cent faster (Notebookcheck), the Snapdragon X version is recalled as a little faster (Ed Tittel), and both ThinkView and Notebookcheck rule out gaming.

highlights.text: curved keys and solid carbon fiber build
almost twelve hours of Wi-Fi battery life

paras: Reviewers mostly recommend it to business users who want a light ThinkPad convertible, praising the keyboard, ports and build. Mixed takes come from performance and price: the Core Ultra 7 155U IPS model trails Snapdragon X, Ryzen AI 9 and Apple M3 laptops (Digital Trends), the Ryzen-powered Dell Inspiron 14 2-in-1 beat it in five of six productivity tests (PCMag UK), and the HP Spectre x360 14 is better value at a similar price (Laptop Mag). Battery results depend on config, from 18 hours 43 minutes in PCMark 10 Modern Office on the Core Ultra 7 155U model (StorageReview) to 8 hours 29 minutes of WiFi browsing on the Core Ultra 7 165U OLED model (Notebookcheck).

highlights.text: better value at a similar price

paras: Reviewers praise the keyboard, the light body of about 2.4 lb and the OLED screen, and the laptop suits business users and frequent travellers. Battery results vary by config and test, from 4 hours 8 minutes in a workday test on the Core Ultra 7 165U with 64GB (Decoding Labs) to 13 hours 2 minutes in PCMark Modern Office on the Core Ultra 7 165U with 32GB (Engadget), while the Core Ultra 7 155H OLED model lasted 9 hours 14 minutes on a Wi-Fi test (Tom's Hardware). The price draws repeated criticism, with the Zenbook 14 OLED called cheaper and faster (Engadget) and the Gen 11 suggested as a cheaper pick (Tom's Hardware, PCMag UK).

Reviewers mostly praise the OLED screen and speakers, and suit it to students, office users and media use rather than demanding games or editing. Battery results vary with the config: Venom's Tech got 6 to 7 hours of basic use on the 32GB 2.8K model, while PCMag UK recorded 17:52 of local video playback on the 16GB 120Hz unit. Speed and heat split opinion too: TechZonical found the 32GB model hot and loud in Filmora editing and pointed to the MacBook Air M5 at similar money (TechZonical), while PCMag UK found the HP Spectre x360 14 edges it in CPU and Photoshop tests (PCMag UK).

Reviewers praise the 165Hz mini-LED screen and six-speaker audio, and it suits creators and occasional gamers who want strong CPU and GPU power. It beat the Dell XPS 16 9640 on performance (Notebookcheck) and costs $1,295 less than the XPS 16 in the RTX 4060 configuration (Digital Trends), though the MacBook Pro 16 with M3 Max is much faster (Digital Trends). Battery is where takes split: the RTX 4050 model reached 8 hours 33 minutes in an office test (Andrew Marc David), while the RTX 4060 model gave 4 to 5 hours of normal work (Ben G Kaiser) and the RTX 4070 model managed 4:30 hours at full brightness (Notebookcheck).

Reviewers who liked it point to long battery life and a quiet, cool aluminum chassis, and Notebookcheck measured 16:41 hours of web surfing at 150 nits on the Snapdragon X Plus unit. Mixed takes come from the 60Hz screen and from sibling comparisons, with the 13.8-inch model called the better buy at similar prices (Notebookcheck) and worth about $100 more (This Is), and the Surface Laptop 7 rated better on screen, trackpad and speakers (Bytes & Bets). The M4 MacBook Air costs $100 more and beats all the Surfaces in many tests (The Verge), while Windows on Arm app gaps still limit photo editors and gamers.

Reviewers praise the long battery life and premium build of the Snapdragon X Elite version, and it suits productivity more than gaming or heavy graphics work. Opinions turn mixed on compatibility and price, with Alex Kidman finding some apps fail on ARM and the price hard to justify, and Notebookcheck finding emulated apps slow and the cores hot under load. On speed, the 32GB model beat the MacBook Air 15-inch (M3) on multi-core but trailed it on single-core and graphics (Live Science), and its Geekbench 6 multicore score of 14,400 was ahead of a Dell XPS 14 at 11,920 (Engadget).

Reviewers who liked it praise the bright 4K mini-LED screen and desktop-class speed, with the RTX 5080 version exporting a 12 minute DaVinci Resolve project in 1 minute 52 seconds against 2 minutes 7 seconds on an i9 14900KS and RTX 5070 desktop (Fenson Lin | Gadgetsu). Mixed takes come from price and screen quirks: the RTX 5080 version showed heavy bloom and tearing without G-Sync, and the MSI Vector A18 HX was rated better value at about a thousand less (GizmoSlipTech), the Gigabyte Aorus Master 16 was suggested for similar performance for less (Laptop Mag), and the 4K panel and $5,000-plus price on RTX 5090 models felt like overkill (Tom's Guide). Battery life swings by test, from 2 hours 33 minutes of web surfing (Laptop Mag) to 8 hours 33 minutes in a slideshow loop (Noteforum), both on the RTX 5080 version, while most reviewers call the fans loud under load.

Reviewers who tested the RTX 4070 version praise its 140W GPU, which is faster than the 2024 Zephyrus G14 at 1080p (PC Gamer), along with the stiff metal build and upgradeable RAM. Mixed takes come from price, since the Blade costs up to $700 more than the OLED G14, so the G14 comes out as the better buy (PC Gamer, The Verge), while Tom's Hardware calls the Blade the best-performing 14-inch gaming laptop but very expensive next to cheaper OLED rivals (Tom's Hardware). Battery life also splits on the same config, with The Verge finding up to four hours and ShortCircuit logging 6 hours 55 minutes.

Reviewers who tested the RTX 5090 versions mostly praise the thin aluminum body and 240Hz OLED (PC Gamer, The Verge), and say it suits buyers with money to spare. Mixed takes come from gaming gains over the 2024 RTX 4090 Blade 16, which The Tech Chap measured at 32% in Cyberpunk at matched 160W with DLSS and ray tracing but only single digits to 18% in other games. Battery also varies: Notebookcheck got 7h 55min of Wi-Fi browsing on an RTX 5090 model, Robeytech got 4 hours 6 minutes of Office Productivity on another, and NotebookcheckReviews found about an hour less battery than the Zephyrus G16 (NotebookcheckReviews).

highlights.text: single digits to 18% in other games

paras: Reviewers praise the solid build, the bright 120Hz display and Galaxy phone integration, and see it suiting students, mobile workers and photo editors. One reviewer picks it over a MacBook Air (Mash IT), while the MacBook Air 13 M4 wins on performance and battery life but trails on display (Notebookcheck), and battery results vary by config, from 10 hours 52 minutes of YouTube on the Core Ultra 256V (Mash IT) to 15 hours 28 minutes in PCMark 10 on the Core Ultra 7 256V (Trusted Reviews). Complaints include soldered RAM and PWM flicker at 240 Hz on the Core Ultra 5 226V model (Notebookcheck), shallow key travel (Trusted Reviews) and only a microSD slot (sakitech).
